- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.75), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish within 3–5 days, model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if 10–15 days of price action shows strong trend, forecast should revert to 1–2% below recent peak or above recent trough.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5), model often overfits recent noise — use 3–5 day moving average or 10-day smoothed trend as anchor for forecast.
